I can see why people appreciate the connectivity, but I stand by my perspective. 

Just because an opinion is widely held doesn't automatically make it correct. When you look at systemic issues—like the rise in adolescent mental health crises coinciding with smartphone and platform adoption, algorithmic amplification of outrage, and the erosion of sustained attention spans—the negative structural impacts run very deep.

Connecting with friends is great, but the business models behind these platforms are engineered to capture attention at almost any psychological cost. That fundamental incentive structure is why I view the net impact as harmful. What specific benefits do the researchers you talked to emphasize?
